This audit opens NEW agent-attemptable frontier work that waits on nothing. Every item names a conversion or info-finding outcome (overlay successBar) and respects live canon: hero is deliberately single-CTA prove-first (S123) so conversion-CTA-splits were deliberately CULLED; breadcrumbs already cover all human content pages (only .ai/ agent pages lack them, correctly); FAQPage JSON-LD already present. The frontier is AI-discoverability + SEO info-finding integrity + cold-cache parse + a11y, not more conversion furniture.

founderEvidence: Live state read at session start: /agents.json is genuinely ABSENT at root despite scripts/build-llms-full-shards.mjs explicitly stating it 'Pairs with /agents.json (CANON-011 sitemap standard)' and a prior archived audit (2026-05-22) flagging the agents.json + llms-full combo as the path to 'the most LLM-citable studio site on the web' — never shipped. .well-known/llms.txt + per-project llms-full shards DO exist, so the AI spine is half-built. Meta-description coverage is 93/110 index.html pages; 17 indexable content pages (faq, brand, careers, changelog, community, contact, cookies, data-deletion, accessibility, games/call-of-doodie, games/index, games/mindframe, games/solara, games/project-unknown, games/gridiron-gm, feedback, feedback/insights) ship with no name=description meta. aria-current appears 0 times in index.html and is not emitted by propagate-nav.mjs. Ambient feature bundle is 58.7KB (vs 50.4KB core); it carries 14 scripts, several page-specific (rank-economy-simulator, social-dashboard-public, security-posture, feedback-decision-board) that parse on every cold load though they self-gate at runtime.

items.summary: The site ships .well-known/llms.txt and per-project llms-full shards but has no /agents.json at root — the one canonical file AI agents and crawlers look for to discover a site's machine-readable surfaces, capabilities, and contact/policy. The AI-discovery spine is half-built and nothing keeps its parts consistent.
items.why: CANON-011's sitemap standard names /agents.json explicitly, and build-llms-full-shards.mjs already advertises a pairing that was never delivered. Info-finding outcome: ChatGPT/Claude/Perplexity and agentic crawlers discover the studio's canonical surfaces (sitemap, llms.txt, llms-full shards, primary CTA, projects, policy) from one well-known entrypoint and cite the studio accurately instead of guessing. The second-order win is integrity: a single contract gate keeps agents.json, llms.txt, the shards, and sitemap.xml mutually consistent so the AI spine can never silently drift as projects flip status.
items.recipe: Add scripts/build-agents-json.mjs that generates /agents.json from the project registry + existing public surfaces (declare: name, description, canonical URLs for sitemap/llms.txt/llms-full, per-SPARKED-project shard URLs, primary CTA /membership/, contact, policy /privacy + /terms, automation disclosure). Wire into npm run build. Add scripts/check-ai-discovery-spine.mjs (build:check gate + --self-test) asserting agents.json exists, is valid JSON, lists every SPARKED project that llms.txt lists, and has no dead internal URLs vs sitemap.xml. Public-safe only.

items.summary: 17 of 110 indexable content pages ship with no name=description meta — including faq, brand, careers, changelog, community, contact, the legal pages, and several game landing pages — so Google synthesizes their SERP snippet from arbitrary on-page text.
items.why: On a public studio site the meta description is the conversion copy that runs in search results before anyone clicks. Info-finding outcome: each affected page gets a unique 120-160 char description written in audience voice, so the SERP snippet reads as intentional and lifts click-through. The durable win is the gate: a structural build:check that fails on any indexable (non-noindex) page missing a description makes this class of drift impossible to reintroduce — the same subtractive-then-structural pattern that locked placeholder orphans (S176) and script relevance (S148).
items.recipe: Backfill unique meta descriptions on the 17 pages (audience voice, no internal vocabulary, name the page's value). Add scripts/check-meta-descriptions.mjs: crawl index.html pages, skip any with <meta name=robots ... noindex>, fail on missing/empty description or length outside ~80-170 chars; include --self-test. Wire into build:check. Where a page is propagator-owned, set the description at the template so re-propagation preserves it.

items.summary: The ambient feature bundle (58.7KB) parses on every cold page load yet carries scripts that only do work on one or two surfaces (rank-economy-simulator, social-dashboard-public, security-posture, feedback-decision-board). S178 split vault-genome-strip out via predicate loading; this is wave 2 of the same subtraction.
items.why: Every KB in the always-parsed feature bundle is parse+compile cost paid by every first-time visitor on the cold-cache critical path, even though these scripts immediately bail when their DOM hook is absent. Speed outcome: moving proven single-surface scripts to ambient-loader predicate loading shrinks the cold-cache feature bundle so the homepage and every content page parse less JS to first interaction, mirroring the S178 genome-strip win. Conditional by design — only scripts proven to gate on a hook present on <=2 pages are split; anything ambiguous stays put (no silent regression on a 999 site).
items.recipe: For each feature-bundle candidate, read the script to find the REAL DOM hook it reads (not one it creates) and grep its presence across HTML. If present on <=2 pages, move the source out of AMBIENT_FEATURE_SOURCES in build-ambient-bundle.mjs and add a matching predicate to assets/ambient-loader.js (mirror the genome-strip entry). Re-run the ambient build + report-ambient-coverage + placement gates. If a candidate cannot be proven single-surface, leave it and log why in the closeout (honest, no forced split).

items.summary: The sitewide nav marks the active link with a CSS .active class only — aria-current appears 0 times — so assistive tech and the accessibility tree never announce which page the visitor is on.
items.why: aria-current=page is the canonical signal for 'you are here' and costs almost nothing. UX/info-finding outcome: screen-reader and keyboard users get an explicit current-location cue while navigating, and the cue stays correct because it is emitted by the same propagator that already renders the nav. It also tightens the existing visual active state into a semantically correct one, closing a real WCAG gap on the brand-anchor site.
items.recipe: In scripts/propagate-nav.mjs, emit aria-current="page" on the nav link whose href matches the page's own path (alongside the existing active class), and re-propagate across all pages. Verify the homepage and a nested page render exactly one aria-current. Add a lightweight assertion to an existing nav/structure gate if cheap.
